root_cause.text: In move_pages_huge_pmd(), the huge zero page path sets src_folio to NULL and then uses folio_mk_pmd(NULL, ...), which either dereferences NULL or produces a bogus PFN, and also reconstructs the destination PMD from scratch, dropping the pmd_special() flag required to identify huge zero pages, leading to refcount corruption.
root_cause.evidence: "In the huge zero page branch, src_folio is NULL, so folio_mk_pmd(NULL, pgprot) passes NULL through folio_pfn() and page_to_pfn(). With SPARSEMEM_VMEMMAP this silently produces a bogus PFN, installing a PMD pointing to non-existent physical memory. ... move_pages_huge_pmd() currently reconstructs the destination PMD in the huge zero page branch, which drops PMD state such as pmd_special() ... vm_normal_page_pmd() can treat the moved huge zero PMD as a normal page and corrupt its refcount." The patch replaces folio_mk_pmd() with move_soft_dirty_pmd() and clear_uffd_wp_pmd() on the original src_pmdval.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix missing preservation of soft-dirty flag and improper handling of userfaultfd write-protect flag when moving huge pages in non-writable path
intent_record.what: In the else branch of move_pages_huge_pmd, replaced assignment of _dst_pmd from folio_mk_pmd(src_folio, dst_vma->vm_page_prot) with two operations: first call move_soft_dirty_pmd(src_pmdval) to propagate the soft-dirty bit, then call clear_uffd_wp_pmd() on the result to clear the userfaultfd write-protect flag.
intent_record.how: Previously, the destination PMD was created from the folio ignoring soft-dirty and uffd-wp bits; now these flags are explicitly handled, preserving soft-dirty tracking and clearing uffd wp during huge page migration in the non-writable case.

grouping_result.intent: Fix missing preservation of soft-dirty flag and improper handling of userfaultfd write-protect flag when moving huge pages in non-writable path

relevance_review.reason: The group addresses soft-dirty and userfaultfd write-protect flag preservation in the non-writable path, while the vulnerability root cause specifically involves the huge zero page path setting src_folio to NULL and misusing folio_mk_pmd, leading to NULL dereference and refcount corruption. The fix in Group 0 does not address the NULL dereference or the huge zero page handling.

Author: Matthew Wilcox (Oracle) <willy@infradead.org>

    Removes five conversions from folio to page.  Also removes both callers of

    removing the confusion between mk_pmd(), mk_huge_pmd() and pmd_mkhuge().

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body shows that when the source PMD is a huge zero page (is_huge_zero_pmd true), src_folio is set to NULL at line 2598. In the else branch at line 2660, folio_mk_pmd(src_folio, dst_vma->vm_page_prot) is called with src_folio = NULL, which is the vulnerable construct described in the root cause. No NULL check or special handling is present; the call will dereference NULL or produce a bogus PMD with missing pmd_special flag, leading to refcount corruption.

commit eb1521dad8f391d3f3b88f589db27a288b55b8ed
Author: Suren Baghdasaryan <surenb@google.com>
Date:   Wed Jan 31 09:56:18 2024 -0800

    userfaultfd: handle zeropage moves by UFFDIO_MOVE
    
    Current implementation of UFFDIO_MOVE fails to move zeropages and returns
    EBUSY when it encounters one.  We can handle them by mapping a zeropage at
    the destination and clearing the mapping at the source.  This is done both
    for ordinary and for huge zeropages.
    
    Link: https://lkml.k

This mk_huge_pmd() does not preserve the pmd_special flag required to identify huge zero pages, leading to refcount corruption as described in the root cause. The vulnerable construct is present and the fix is absent.
